text: You grab your phone to watch a video, holding it upright. You anticipate that satisfying full-screen flip.
You turn it sideways, and poof, the screen rotates. But then, a slight shift, and it flips back. Or sometimes, it just refuses to turn.
Why does it feel so random? Is it just gravity? You try to force it, but it stubbornly stays wrong, causing frustration.
Your phone isn't just sensing gravity. It uses internal sensors – accelerometers and gyroscopes – to detect its exact angle, applying programmed rules.
These rules anticipate your intent: portrait for browsing, landscape for media. But its best guess often misses your specific desire, causing friction.
So, next time your screen resists, remember: it's an invisible system predicting your action. Sometimes, its calculated guess is just plain wrong.
